title: Sandbox basics
description: A full tour of the connected Sandbox: every signer of its good chain in PAdES, CAdES and XAdES; each of its TSAs; CRLs over HTTP, HTTPS and LDAP and its OCSP responder, with every failure they can be switched to; revocations made on demand; short-lived certificates; its trusted list; and the cases a signer must refuse or a validator must not accept. Only generic policies (sandbox-strict, the library's default validation): what a trust framework's profile or policy decides is in that framework's playbook.

sections.title: Signers of the good chain
sections.description: Every key the Sandbox issues under its intermediate CA signs with the strict policy.

steps.title: RSA 2048, B-B
steps.description: Signs the sample contract in PAdES B-B with the Sandbox's RSA 2048 signer under the strict policy (chain and revocation checked before signing). The reference signature: later steps validate and augment its file.

steps.title: RSA 3072
steps.description: Signs with the RSA 3072 key of the good chain, to show the strict policy accepts it like RSA 2048.

steps.title: RSA 4096
steps.description: Signs with the RSA 4096 key of the good chain, to show larger RSA keys are accepted.

steps.title: ECDSA P-256
steps.description: Signs with an ECDSA P-256 key, to show elliptic-curve signers of the good chain are accepted.

steps.title: ECDSA P-384
steps.description: Signs with an ECDSA P-384 key (the curve is matched with SHA-384).

steps.title: ECDSA P-521
steps.description: Signs with an ECDSA P-521 key, the largest NIST curve; its file is validated further down.

steps.title: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-512
steps.description: Signs with RSA 2048 using RSASSA-PSS padding and SHA-512 instead of PKCS#1 v1.5, to show the algorithm override produces a signature the policy accepts.

steps.title: Validate the RSA 2048 signature
steps.description: Validates the RSA 2048 B-B file with the Sandbox as trust anchor: an intact signature by a valid, unrevoked certificate must give TOTAL_PASSED.

steps.title: Validate the ECDSA P-521 signature
steps.description: Validates the ECDSA P-521 file, to show the validator handles the P-521 curve and its signature encoding.

sections.title: PAdES, CAdES and XAdES up to B-LTA
sections.description: The three formats at B-LT and B-LTA through the Sandbox's TSA, CRLs and OCSP, each validated afterwards.

steps.title: PAdES B-LT
steps.description: Also validated by EU DSS when one is connected (crossValidate); without DSS the step still runs and says so.

steps.title: Validate the PAdES B-LT signature
steps.description: Validates the PAdES B-LT file: the signature time-stamp and the CRL/OCSP data embedded in its DSS must be enough to reach TOTAL_PASSED.

steps.title: PAdES B-LTA
steps.description: Signs in PAdES B-LTA: a signature time-stamp, the validation data in the DSS and a document time-stamp over it, so the signature can be verified after its certificates expire.

steps.title: Validate the PAdES B-LTA signature (archival data)
steps.description: Validates the B-LTA file at the archival-data level, which also checks the document time-stamp and the data it protects.

steps.title: Augment the B-B signature to B-LTA
steps.description: Raises the B-B signature of sign-basic to B-LTA without signing again (adds a time-stamp, validation data and a document time-stamp in incremental updates), as a preservation service would.

steps.title: CAdES B-LT, detached
steps.description: Signs the sample text in CAdES B-LT, detached (the signature is a .p7s apart from the data), with the time-stamp and the revocation data in the unsigned attributes.

steps.title: CAdES B-LTA, enveloped, ECDSA P-384
steps.description: Signs in CAdES B-LTA with the data inside the signature (enveloped) and an ECDSA P-384 key, adding the archive time-stamp.

steps.title: Validate the CAdES B-LT signature
steps.description: Validates the detached CAdES B-LT signature; as it carries no content, the original text is given alongside (dataId).

steps.title: Validate the CAdES B-LTA signature
steps.description: Validates the enveloped CAdES B-LTA signature, archive time-stamp included; the content is inside, so no data is given.

steps.title: XAdES B-LT, enveloped
steps.description: Signs the sample XML order in XAdES B-LT, enveloped (the signature goes inside the document), with the time-stamp and the revocation data.

steps.title: XAdES B-LTA, enveloping, ECDSA P-256
steps.description: Signs in XAdES B-LTA, enveloping (the data goes inside the signature), with an ECDSA P-256 key and an archive time-stamp.

steps.title: Validate the XAdES B-LT signature
steps.description: Validates the enveloped XAdES B-LT file and its time-stamp and revocation data.

steps.title: Validate the XAdES B-LTA signature
steps.description: Validates the enveloping XAdES B-LTA file, archive time-stamp included.

steps.title: XAdES B-LTA, detached
steps.description: XAdES B-LTA detached: the signature references the XML document from outside, and its archive time-stamp covers that reference; the third XAdES form, next to enveloped and enveloping.

sections.title: Time-stamping authorities
sections.description: Each TSA endpoint of the Sandbox and each failure its TSA can be switched to.

steps.title: TSA (/tsa/tsr), the expected one
steps.description: Signs at B-T with the Sandbox's main TSA, naming it as the expected TSA (expectedTsa): the token comes from the TSA the signer was configured to trust, so the signature is made.

steps.title: TSA with HTTP Basic (/tsa/authenticated)
steps.description: Gets the time-stamp from the TSA endpoint that requires HTTP Basic authentication, to show the credentials are sent and the token accepted.

steps.title: TSA with a short-lived certificate
steps.description: Gets the time-stamp from a TSA whose certificate is issued for the request and valid 30 more seconds: still valid when the token is checked, so the B-T signature is made (the token will outlive it; only an archive time-stamp would keep it trusted).

steps.title: CAdES B-T with a content timestamp
steps.description: Signs in CAdES B-T and also time-stamps the content before signing (content-time-stamp attribute), which proves the data existed before the signature.

steps.title: XAdES B-T with a data objects timestamp
steps.description: Signs in XAdES B-T with an AllDataObjectsTimeStamp over the signed data, besides the signature time-stamp.

steps.title: Not the TSA the signer expects
steps.description: The signer expects the tokens of another TSA (expectedTsa: tsa-revoked) but gets the main TSA's: the library must refuse (TimestampUntrusted) instead of embedding a time-stamp from an authority it was not told to use.

steps.title: TSA whose certificate is revoked (/tsa/revoked)
steps.description: The TSA's certificate is revoked: a token it signs proves nothing, so the signer must refuse (TimestampCertificateRevoked).

steps.title: TSA whose certificate expired (/tsa/expired)
steps.description: The TSA's certificate has expired: the signer must refuse its token (TimestampCertificateNotValid).

steps.title: TSA outside every trust anchor
steps.description: The TSA's certificate does not chain to any trust anchor: its token must be refused (TimestampUntrusted).

steps.title: TSA whose tokens name another TSA
steps.description: The checks before signing look at the TSA's chain, not at the tsa field of its tokens: the signature is made, and the validator flags the name.

steps.title: Validate it: the TSA name does not match its certificate
steps.description: Validates the file of tsa-wrong-name with a policy that makes TSAGeneralNameContentMatch fail: the name in the token's tsa field does not match the TSA certificate, and the report must say which constraint failed.

steps.title: TSA down
steps.description: The TSA does not answer: a B-T signature cannot be made, so the signer must fail instead of quietly returning B-B.

steps.title: TSA down, signing at the highest level reached
steps.description: The TSA is down but the caller allows a lower level (returnLowerLevel): the signature is made at B-B, the highest level reached, and says so.

steps.title: TSA slow (3 s)
steps.description: The TSA answers after 3 seconds: within the client's timeout, so the B-T signature is still made.

steps.title: TSA answers a corrupted token
steps.description: The TSA answers a corrupted token: the signer must detect it and refuse instead of embedding it.

steps.title: TSA answers a token signed outside every trust anchor
steps.description: The TSA answers a well-formed token signed by a key outside every trust anchor: it must be refused (TimestampUntrusted).

steps.title: CAdES: TSA whose certificate is revoked
steps.description: The revoked TSA in CAdES: the token is checked before it is kept whatever the format, so the signature is refused (TimestampCertificateRevoked).

steps.title: XAdES: TSA whose certificate is revoked
steps.description: The revoked TSA in XAdES: the token is checked before it is kept whatever the format, so the signature is refused (TimestampCertificateRevoked).

steps.title: CAdES: TSA whose certificate expired
steps.description: The expired TSA in CAdES: the token is checked before it is kept whatever the format, so the signature is refused (TimestampCertificateNotValid).

steps.title: XAdES: TSA whose certificate expired
steps.description: The expired TSA in XAdES: the token is checked before it is kept whatever the format, so the signature is refused (TimestampCertificateNotValid).

sections.title: CRLs over HTTP, HTTPS and LDAP
sections.description: Certificates whose only revocation source is a CRL, and every failure the CRL server can be switched to.

steps.title: Good, CRL over HTTPS
steps.description: Signs with a certificate whose only revocation source is a CRL over HTTPS: the CRL is fetched over TLS, says good, and the signature is made. Its file is validated later with the CRL server failing.

steps.title: Revoked, CRL over HTTPS
steps.description: A certificate listed as revoked in the HTTPS CRL (no OCSP to fall back to): the signer must refuse (CertificateRevoked).

steps.title: Good, CRL over LDAP
steps.description: Signs with a certificate whose only CRL distribution point is an ldap:// URL, to show the CRL is read from the directory.

steps.title: Revoked, CRL over LDAP
steps.description: A certificate listed as revoked in the LDAP CRL: the signer must refuse (CertificateRevoked).

steps.title: B-LT with the CRL fetched over HTTPS
steps.description: Signs at B-LT with the HTTPS-CRL certificate: the CRL fetched over HTTPS goes into the signature's validation data.

steps.title: Validate the B-LT signature with its embedded CRL
steps.description: Validates that B-LT file: the CRL embedded in it must be enough to reach TOTAL_PASSED.

steps.title: CRL server down, no OCSP
steps.description: The CRL server is down and the certificate has no OCSP: its status cannot be known, and the strict policy refuses (RevocationStatusUnknown) instead of signing blind.

steps.title: LDAP directory busy, no OCSP
steps.description: The LDAP directory refuses to answer for a certificate whose only CRL is there: the status is unknown, so the signer refuses (RevocationStatusUnknown).

steps.title: CRL server slow (3 s)
steps.description: The CRL server answers after 3 seconds: within the timeout, so the status is known and the signature made.

steps.title: CRL past its nextUpdate
steps.description: The CRL served is past its nextUpdate: stale revocation data is not proof of a current status, so the signer refuses (RevocationStatusUnknown).

steps.title: CRL signed by another key
steps.description: The CRL is signed by a key other than its issuer's: it cannot be trusted, so the status is unknown and the signer refuses.

steps.title: CRL without nextUpdate
steps.description: The CRL has no nextUpdate: the strict policy (CRLNextUpdatePresent at FAIL) does not accept it, so the signer refuses (RevocationStatusUnknown).

steps.title: Revoked after the CRL a client may have cached
steps.description: The CRL served predates the revocation; the OCSP responder already knows it.

steps.title: Validate a B-B signature when the CRL is signed by another key
steps.description: Validates the B-B file of crl-https-good while the CRL is signed by another key: with no revocation data to trust and none embedded, the result must be INDETERMINATE, not valid.

steps.title: Validate a B-B signature when the CRL has expired
steps.description: Validates the B-B file of crl-https-good while the CRL served is past its nextUpdate and there is no OCSP: no current revocation data, so the validator gives no verdict (INDETERMINATE) instead of valid.

sections.title: OCSP responder
sections.description: Certificates whose only revocation source is OCSP, every failure the responder can be switched to, and the fallback between OCSP and CRL.

steps.title: Good, OCSP only
steps.description: Signs with a certificate whose only revocation source is the OCSP responder: it answers good, and the signature is made.

steps.title: Revoked, OCSP only
steps.description: The OCSP responder answers revoked: the signer must refuse (CertificateRevoked).

steps.title: B-LT with the OCSP response embedded
steps.description: Signs at B-LT with the OCSP-only certificate: the OCSP response goes into the signature's validation data.

steps.title: Validate the B-LT signature with its embedded OCSP response
steps.description: Validates that B-LT file using the OCSP response embedded in it.

steps.title: Responder down
steps.description: The responder is down and the certificate has no CRL: the status is unknown, so the signer refuses (RevocationStatusUnknown).

steps.title: Responder slow (3 s)
steps.description: The responder answers after 3 seconds: within the timeout, so the signature is made.

steps.title: Responder answers tryLater
steps.description: The responder answers tryLater (no status): the signer must treat it as unknown and refuse.

steps.title: Response past its nextUpdate
steps.description: The OCSP response is past its nextUpdate: not acceptable as current status, so the signer refuses.

steps.title: Response signed by an unauthorized responder
steps.description: The response is signed by a responder its CA did not authorize (no id-kp-OCSPSigning delegation): it must be ignored, so the status is unknown and the signer refuses.

steps.title: Responder answers unknown
steps.description: The responder answers unknown for the certificate: not proof of good status, so the signer refuses.

steps.title: OCSP down, the CRL answers
steps.description: OCSP is preferred but down: the signer must fall back to the CRL, which answers good, and sign.

steps.title: CRL down, OCSP answers
steps.description: The CRL is preferred but down: the signer must fall back to OCSP, which answers good, and sign.

steps.title: B-LT with OCSP down: the CRL is embedded
steps.description: B-LT with OCSP down: the CRL the signer fell back to is what gets embedded as validation data.

steps.title: OCSP and CRL both down
steps.description: Neither OCSP nor the CRL answers: no revocation source is left, so the signer must refuse (RevocationStatusUnknown).

steps.title: Validate a B-B signature with OCSP and CRL down
steps.description: Validates the B-B file of sign-basic with OCSP and CRL down: without revocation data the validator cannot conclude, so INDETERMINATE.

sections.title: Revoked chains and revocations on demand
sections.description: Certificates the Sandbox issues revoked, and good ones revoked for a single step and put back after it.

steps.title: Revoked in the CRL and by OCSP
steps.description: A certificate the Sandbox issues already revoked, in its CRL and by OCSP: the signer must refuse (CertificateRevoked).

steps.title: Under a revoked CA
steps.description: A good end-entity certificate under an intermediate CA that is revoked: the whole chain is checked, so the signer must refuse.

steps.title: Revoked, CAdES
steps.description: The revoked certificate again, in CAdES: the refusal does not depend on the format.

steps.title: Revoked, XAdES
steps.description: The revoked certificate again, in XAdES: same refusal.

steps.title: Good certificate revoked for this step
steps.description: The Sandbox revokes the good RSA 3072 certificate for this step only: the signer must see the new revocation (no stale cache) and refuse.

steps.title: The same certificate after the step put it back
steps.description: The same RSA 3072 certificate after the previous step's revocation was undone: it signs again, showing the Sandbox puts its state back between steps.

steps.title: OCSP-only certificate revoked for this step
steps.description: Revokes the OCSP-only certificate for this step: the responder must report it at once and the signer refuse.

steps.title: LDAP-only certificate revoked for this step
steps.description: Revokes the LDAP-CRL-only certificate for this step: the CRL in the directory must list it and the signer refuse.

steps.title: B-T signature to revoke later
steps.description: Signs at B-T with ECDSA P-384: the signature time-stamp is the proof of existence used by the next step, which revokes this certificate.

steps.title: Revoked after its time-stamp: still valid
steps.description: Two seconds later, revokes the ECDSA P-384 certificate and validates the B-T file: the time-stamp proves the signature existed before the revocation, so it stays valid.

sections.title: Validity, key usage and algorithms
sections.description: Certificates the strict policy must refuse before signing (expired, not yet valid, under an expired or SHA-1 CA, weak key, wrong key usage) and the one it accepts (no nonRepudiation).

steps.title: Expired certificate
steps.description: A certificate past its notAfter: the signer must refuse (CertificateExpired).

steps.title: Not yet valid
steps.description: A certificate whose notBefore is in the future: the signer must refuse (CertificateNotCurrentlyValid).

steps.title: Under an expired CA
steps.description: A valid end-entity certificate under an expired intermediate CA: the chain is not valid now, so the signer refuses (ChainCertificateNotValid).

steps.title: Under a CA signed with SHA-1
steps.description: A certificate under a CA whose certificate is signed with SHA-1: the strict policy checks the algorithms of the CA certificates too (CACertificate/Cryptographic), so it refuses (AlgorithmNotPermitted).

steps.title: RSA 1024
steps.description: An RSA 1024 key, below the policy's minimum size: the signer must refuse (KeyTooWeak).

steps.title: Key usage keyEncipherment only
steps.description: A certificate whose key usage allows only keyEncipherment: it is not meant for signatures, so the signer refuses (KeyUsageNotPermitted).

steps.title: No key usage extension
steps.description: A certificate without the key usage extension: the strict policy requires one allowing signatures, so the signer refuses.

steps.title: digitalSignature without nonRepudiation
steps.description: A certificate with digitalSignature but not nonRepudiation: the strict policy accepts digitalSignature alone, so the signature is made (IOFE-style policies that require nonRepudiation would refuse it).

steps.title: CAdES: key usage keyEncipherment only
steps.description: The certificate not meant for signing, in CAdES: the key usage check does not depend on the format, so it is refused the same way (KeyUsageNotPermitted).

steps.title: XAdES: key usage keyEncipherment only
steps.description: The certificate not meant for signing, in XAdES: the key usage check does not depend on the format, so it is refused the same way (KeyUsageNotPermitted).

steps.title: CAdES: RSA 1024
steps.description: An RSA 1024 key in CAdES: refused as in PAdES (KeyTooWeak), whatever the format.

steps.title: XAdES: RSA 1024
steps.description: An RSA 1024 key in XAdES: refused as in PAdES (KeyTooWeak), whatever the format.

sections.title: Short-lived certificates
sections.description: Signers issued when the step runs, valid for 20 seconds: a B-LTA signature outlives its certificate, a B-B one does not.

steps.title: B-LTA with a 20-second certificate
steps.description: The Sandbox issues a certificate valid for 20 seconds and the step signs at B-LTA with it, while it is still valid.

steps.title: B-B with a 20-second certificate
steps.description: Another 20-second certificate signs at B-B: no time-stamp or validation data, so nothing will prove the signature was made while the certificate was valid.

steps.title: The B-LTA signature after its certificate expired
steps.description: After 25 seconds, when the certificate has expired, validates the B-LTA file: its time-stamps and embedded validation data prove it was signed in time, so TOTAL_PASSED.

steps.title: The B-B signature after its certificate expired
steps.description: Validates the B-B file after its certificate expired: with no proof of existence the validator cannot place the signature inside the validity period (OUT_OF_BOUNDS_NO_POE).

sections.title: Trust anchors and the trusted list
sections.description: The Sandbox's root, its trusted list (/tl/tl.xml) and every failure the list can be switched to, before signing and when validating.

steps.title: Chain to the Sandbox root
steps.description: Signs with the Sandbox root as the only trust anchor: the chain reaches it, so the signature is made.

steps.title: Chain to the trusted list
steps.description: Signs with the anchors taken from the Sandbox's trusted list (/tl/tl.xml) instead of a configured root: the list is fetched, its signature checked and its CAs used.

steps.title: Validate with the trusted list as anchors
steps.description: Validates that file with the trusted list as the trust anchors.

steps.title: Trusted list past its NextUpdate
steps.description: The trusted list is past its NextUpdate: an outdated list cannot give trust, so there is no anchor and the signer refuses (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: Trusted list signed by another operator
steps.description: The trusted list is signed by a certificate other than its operator's: it must not be used, so the signer refuses (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: Trusted list changed after it was signed
steps.description: The trusted list was changed after it was signed (its XML signature breaks): it must not be used, so the signer refuses.

steps.title: Validate when the trusted list has another signer
steps.description: Validates the trust-list file while the list has another signer: without trusted anchors the validator cannot conclude (INDETERMINATE).

steps.title: B-T signature trusted through the list
steps.description: Signs at B-T trusting the list: the time-stamp is the proof of existence for the withdrawal steps that follow.

steps.title: Root withdrawn from the list: a new signature is refused
steps.description: The list now withdraws the root from service: a new signature has no anchor, so the signer refuses (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: Root withdrawn after the time-stamp: still valid
steps.description: Validates the B-T file of trust-list-history after the root was withdrawn: the list's history shows the root was granted when the time-stamp was made, so the signature stays valid.

sections.title: Validation of the Sandbox samples
sections.description: The signed samples made with the Sandbox's certificates: what a validator must accept and what it must not.

steps.title: Valid
steps.description: Validates the bundled valid sample: TOTAL_PASSED, and the ETSI TS 119 102-2 report must be valid against its XML schema.

steps.title: Revoked signer
steps.description: Validates the sample signed by a revoked certificate without a time-stamp: no proof it was signed before the revocation, so REVOKED_NO_POE.

steps.title: Expired signer
steps.description: Validates the sample signed by an expired certificate without a time-stamp: OUT_OF_BOUNDS_NO_POE.

steps.title: Root outside the trust anchors
steps.description: Validates the sample whose chain ends at a root outside the anchors: NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND, never valid.

steps.title: Content changed after signing
steps.description: Validates the sample whose content changed after signing: the digest does not match, so TOTAL_FAILED.

steps.title: CAdES: data changed
steps.description: Validates a detached CAdES signature against data that changed after signing: HASH_FAILURE.

steps.title: XAdES: data changed
steps.description: Validates an XAdES file whose signed data changed: the reference digest fails, HASH_FAILURE.
